criteria.description: identity.sanitize_user_id is the chosen mechanism (NOT a separate registry module) and it rejects '_shared' as a user_id, so no minted/resolvable user can alias the shared namespace. '_shared' currently passes the existing charset regex [a-z0-9_-]+, so this is a genuine new check added at the identity boundary. The reservation lives at the identity boundary (sanitize_user_id); the document helpers are NOT expected to independently re-reject '_shared'.
criteria.verifyBy: A pinned test in the identity test module asserts sanitize_user_id('_shared') is rejected per the existing convention (returns None / falsy, matching how other invalid ids are handled), while a plain id like 'matt' still passes through unchanged. Run with .venv/bin/python -m pytest.

criteria.description: A document seeded in documents/_shared/ appears in list_documents(user_id) for two or more distinct users (e.g. 'matt' and 'sarah', plus a third user). list_documents signature is unchanged — still list_documents(user_id).
criteria.verifyBy: Pure-helper test (no TestClient) in tests/test_documents_list_load.py using conftest-monkeypatched docs_dir: seed a doc under _shared/, assert its doc_id is present in list_documents('matt'), list_documents('sarah'), and a third user (using the existing asyncio.run pattern for the async helper).

criteria.description: Each user's own uploads remain invisible to other users after adding the shared union — the existing mirror-image isolation behavior is preserved. A doc under documents/<userA>/ does NOT appear in list_documents(userB).
criteria.verifyBy: Extend mirror-image test in tests/test_documents_list_load.py: seed a per-user doc for 'matt', assert it appears in list_documents('matt') but NOT in list_documents('sarah'); and vice versa. Existing document isolation tests stay green.

criteria.description: list_documents de-duplicates on shadow collision keyed on doc_id: when a user has their own doc with the same doc_id as a shared doc, list_documents(user_id) returns that doc_id EXACTLY ONCE, as the user's version (matching load-resolution), not as a duplicate picker entry.
criteria.verifyBy: Test in tests/test_documents_list_load.py: seed doc_id 'D' with distinct content/title under both documents/<matt>/ and documents/_shared/; assert list_documents('matt') contains exactly one entry whose id == 'D' and whose title/metadata are matt's (not the shared one).

criteria.description: Backward-compat when _shared/ is absent: with no documents/_shared/ directory present, list_documents behavior is unchanged — a fresh user with no uploads gets [], and existing users get only their own docs. The shared union must be keyed strictly on _shared/ presence so it does not regress the empty/absent-_shared path.
criteria.verifyBy: Test: with no _shared/ dir seeded, assert list_documents('dev') == [] for a fresh user and that a user with only their own docs sees exactly those. The existing test_documents_are_user_scoped (which asserts an empty list for a fresh 'dev' user while other users' dirs exist) stays green.

criteria.description: No minted/resolvable user_id can equal '_shared': because sanitize_user_id rejects '_shared' (c1), the union inside list_documents is the ONLY surface through which documents/_shared/ contents reach a user's picker. The document helpers do not independently reject '_shared'; the reservation is enforced solely at the identity boundary, so shared docs surface exclusively via the union for a real minted user.
criteria.verifyBy: Executable test: (a) assert sanitize_user_id('_shared') is rejected (falsy), demonstrating no resolvable identity can be '_shared'; and (b) seed a doc in documents/_shared/ and assert it appears via list_documents('matt') (the union path). Concrete pass/fail; no reviewer judgment.

criteria.description: load_document(user_id, doc_id) resolves the user's own namespace first, then falls back to _shared/ on miss. A shared doc loads successfully for two different users. Signature unchanged: load_document(user_id, doc_id).
criteria.verifyBy: Pure-helper test: seed a doc only in _shared/, assert load_document('matt', shared_id) and load_document('sarah', shared_id) both return non-None content matching the seeded doc.

criteria.description: load_document(user_id, doc_id) still returns None for a doc that belongs to another user and is not in _shared/ (cross-user isolation for load unchanged).
criteria.verifyBy: Test: seed a doc only under documents/<sarah>/, assert load_document('matt', sarahs_doc_id) returns None.

criteria.description: Shadowing is deterministic for load: when a user has their own doc with the same doc_id as a shared doc, load_document(user_id, doc_id) returns the USER's doc, not the shared one.
criteria.verifyBy: Test: seed doc_id 'D' with distinct content under both documents/<matt>/ and documents/_shared/; assert load_document('matt', 'D') returns matt's content, while load_document('sarah', 'D') (no own copy) returns the shared content.

criteria.description: save_upload(user_id, ...) NEVER writes to documents/_shared/ — uploads always land in the acting user's namespace directory, and a pre-existing _shared/ is left byte-for-byte unchanged. This holds both for normal users AND closes the aliasing hole: because sanitize_user_id rejects '_shared' at the identity boundary (c1), save_upload is never reached with user_id='_shared', so the app has no write path into _shared/ at all. Signature unchanged: save_upload(user_id, ...).
criteria.verifyBy: Test: pre-seed documents/_shared/ with a sentinel doc; snapshot the _shared/ directory contents (filenames + bytes); call save_upload for two different users; assert (a) each user's saved file exists under documents/<user_id>/, (b) the _shared/ snapshot is unchanged (same filenames, same bytes, no new entries). Additionally assert that sanitize_user_id('_shared') is falsy (c1) so no request can drive save_upload with '_shared' as the acting user — pinning that the aliasing write-path is closed upstream.

criteria.description: No signature changes to the touched document helpers: list_documents(user_id), load_document(user_id, doc_id), save_upload(user_id, ...) keep their exact existing signatures; and list_documents remains a coroutine. The shared namespace is an internal resolution fallback only.
criteria.verifyBy: inspect.signature checks in a test confirming parameter names/order unchanged from pre-sprint for all three helpers; plus assert asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(list_documents) is True (async-ness preserved); plus all existing call sites remain valid.

criteria.description: The full existing test suite stays green, including the mirror-image isolation suite and the pinned static_prompt_hash literals; bot.py prompt content is untouched.
criteria.verifyBy: Run .venv/bin/python -m pytest (full suite) and confirm all tests pass with no modifications to bot.py prompt content.

scope.description: Code changes limited to documents.py (shared-namespace resolution fallback + list union/dedup) and a single reserved-name guard in identity.sanitize_user_id. No other production modules edited.
No changes to route/endpoint signatures, identity.py cookie logic (beyond the _shared rejection in sanitize_user_id), or bot.py static prompt content.

claims.py shared-sidecar behavior, per-user state modules (sessions/recaps/study history), UI/picker labeling, migration scripts, and copying actual demo documents into _shared/ are out of scope for this sprint (Sprint 0 covers document resolution + list union/dedup + save_upload + the _shared name reservation only).

Tests are pure-helper only (no TestClient), extend the existing mirror-image patterns, and use conftest monkeypatched path constants (docs_dir); no files are deleted; pipecat stays pinned; nothing pushed or merged (run branch only).
